written: before any world-state code was written and before any passage was authored, rendered or rated
question: Does a persistent WORLD STATE (stable object ids, owner / location, deeds that change them, the result kept on screen in the following beats) let a muted viewer read who did what to which object and where it is now, better than the current engine?

arms.A: current engine (origin/god-mode e837a6cb renderer) — the passage authored with today's vocabulary only: per-beat cast, action (take / place / hold / reach / offer ...), holds, props; written by the same author in the same session as B
arms.B: the same beats, same narration, same timing, same shots and cast, authored with the prototype's world declarations (objects with id / owner / location; per-beat deeds) compiled by the prototype into the scene; the prototype renderer draws resting objects at their location and keeps every object where its last deed left it
arms.same: one Remotion bundle renders both arms (B's renderer path is opt-in per config, so A is drawn exactly as today); captions off; identical frame times

passages.rule: narration beats in committed Antidote books (books/*/art.json + config.antidote.json) where a person physically moves a concrete object (verb + object noun regex, scratchpad c10/find-transfers.js, 30 hits), minus hypothetical / rhetorical / metaphorical uses (judged on the narration text only, before authoring); each passage = the event beat with one beat of context so the sequence shows before -> deed -> after

selected.event: phone on the nightstand -> grabbed -> in hand, screen lit (52 unread)
sword hangs on the wall -> taken off the wall -> carried out the door
box held on the palm -> hand pulled away -> box falls, lies on the floor
mug cupped in the hands -> kept in hand while it cools
notebook open on the desk -> takes a pen -> rules a line in the notebook
the Davis family keep their money -> handed over -> Buffett holds it
bag beside the person -> grabbed -> carried away to the elevator
card in the person's hand -> handed over to the friend -> the friend has it
reader holds the book -> puts the book down -> book on the table, reader leaves it
phone in hand -> put down -> on the table, hand free

passages.excluded: the-new-one-minute-manager 149 (hypothetical), creativity 101 (rhetorical), buffett 166 (metaphor: cash out of a company), learned-optimism 23/25 (animals, not a hand object), wonder 229 / surrounded-by-idiots 57 / 114 / as-good-as-dead 22 / nobody-wants 57 / 127 / 15-secrets 162 (idiom), 15-secrets 68 and stolen-focus 183 (generic habit, already covered by P01 / P10), burn-of-the-everflame 164 (touch, no state change)

stimulus: per passage x arm ONE 3-frame strip: the three beats at 75 % of each beat (after the default action cue at 40 %), left to right, caption layer off; plus the three single frames for the standard rubric

raters.describer: a FRESH sonnet agent per strip, never shown both arms of a passage, never the narration: describes the three frames, then answers: who acts (which figure), what object, who / where had it in frame 1, who / where has it in frame 3, what changed, what follows from it
raters.judge: a FRESH sonnet agent per passage-arm: the narration of the three beats + the description only (no image); scores each state question CORRECT / WRONG / NOT_SHOWN against the narration, and the standard mute rubric per frame (CORRECT / NEUTRAL / WRONG; ADDS / TEXT_ONLY / NONE; EXPLAINS YES / NO) — JUDGE_RULES verbatim (scripts/lib/mute-rubric.js)
raters.replicates: 2 independent describer+judge replicates per strip (cycle 8: describer variance is high)
raters.human: a blind human rating sheet (strips shuffled, arm hidden) is produced for the operator; its result is reported separately when filled — the agent result is never presented as human judgement

measures.stateComprehension: per strip: the share of the 6 state questions (actor, object, before-holder/location, after-holder/location, change, consequence) judged CORRECT
measures.rubric: WRONG, DEAD (contribution NONE), ADDS, EXPLAINS over the 3 frames of each strip
measures.integrity: teleportation (object at a place it never reached by a deed) and duplication (one object drawn twice) counted by the compiler on B and by inspection of the strips on both arms

all: stateComprehension(B) - stateComprehension(A) >= +20 percentage points (pooled over passages and replicates)
shipRule.else: NO SHIP (the prototype stays on its branch)
shipRule.uncertainty: paired bootstrap 95 % interval over passages (10) for the comprehension difference; with n = 10 the result is a pilot signal, never a general claim
shipRule.scope: an experiment criterion, never a production gate; nothing reaches production without the operator
